# quay_repository_notification (Resource)

Manages a notification on a Quay repository. Because the Quay API has no update endpoint for notifications, any change to notification attributes will cause the existing notification to be deleted and a new one created. Exactly one method block (webhook, slack, email, or quay_notification) must be provided. Exactly one event block must be provided; event-specific configuration (such as the vulnerability severity level or a build ref regex) lives inside that block.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "quay_organization" "example" {
  name  = "my-org"
  email = "admin@example.com"
}

resource "quay_repository" "example" {
  namespace  = quay_organization.example.name
  name       = "my-app"
  visibility = "private"
}

# Webhook triggered on every image push
resource "quay_repository_notification" "push_webhook" {
  repository = quay_repository.example.id
  title      = "Push notification"

  webhook   = { url = "https://hooks.example.com/quay" }
  repo_push = {}
}

# Slack alert for build failures
resource "quay_repository_notification" "build_failure_slack" {
  repository = quay_repository.example.id
  title      = "Build failure alert"

  slack         = { url = "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T00000/B00000/XXXXXXXXXXXX" }
  build_failure = {}
}

# Webhook for High severity (and above) vulnerability findings
resource "quay_repository_notification" "vuln_webhook" {
  repository = quay_repository.example.id
  title      = "High+ vulnerability alert"

  webhook             = { url = "https://hooks.example.com/vulns" }
  vulnerability_found = { level = "High" }
}

# Email notification for main-branch build successes only
resource "quay_repository_notification" "main_build_email" {
  repository = quay_repository.example.id
  title      = "Main branch build succeeded"

  email         = { email = "team@example.com" }
  build_success = { ref_regex = "refs/heads/main" }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the repository.
- `namespace` (String) The namespace (organization or username) that owns the repository.

### Optional

- `build_cancelled` (Attributes) Trigger when a build is cancelled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--build_cancelled))
- `build_failure` (Attributes) Trigger when a build fails. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--build_failure))
- `build_queued` (Attributes) Trigger when a build is queued. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--build_queued))
- `build_start` (Attributes) Trigger when a build starts. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--build_start))
- `build_success` (Attributes) Trigger when a build succeeds. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--build_success))
- `email` (Attributes) Deliver notifications by email. The address must already be authorized and confirmed for the repository in the Quay UI before this resource is created; Quay rejects unverified addresses with 400 "not authorized to receive notifications" and the provider cannot run the confirmation flow. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--email))
- `quay_notification` (Attributes) Deliver notifications as in-app alerts in the Quay web UI to a specific user or team. The recipient must be a member of the repository's namespace. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--quay_notification))
- `repo_image_expiry` (Attributes) Trigger when an image in the repository is due to expire. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--repo_image_expiry))
- `repo_mirror_sync_failed` (Attributes) Trigger when a repository mirror sync fails. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--repo_mirror_sync_failed))
- `repo_mirror_sync_started` (Attributes) Trigger when a repository mirror sync starts. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--repo_mirror_sync_started))
- `repo_mirror_sync_success` (Attributes) Trigger when a repository mirror sync succeeds. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--repo_mirror_sync_success))
- `repo_push` (Attributes) Trigger on every image push to the repository. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--repo_push))
- `slack` (Attributes) Deliver notifications to a Slack channel via an Incoming Webhook URL. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--slack))
- `title` (String) A human-readable title for the notification.
- `vulnerability_found` (Attributes) Trigger when a vulnerability is found. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vulnerability_found))
- `webhook` (Attributes) Deliver notifications via an HTTP POST to a URL. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--webhook))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier (repository/uuid).
- `number_of_failures` (Number) The number of consecutive delivery failures.
- `uuid` (String) The server-assigned UUID of the notification.

### Nested Schema for `quay_notification.target`

Required:

- `name` (String) The Quay username or team name to notify.

Required:

- `days` (Number) Trigger the notification when the image will expire within this many days.

<a id="nestedatt--slack"></a>
### Nested Schema for `slack`

Required:

- `url` (String, Sensitive) The Slack Incoming Webhook URL. Marked sensitive because the URL itself is the credential.


<a id="nestedatt--vulnerability_found"></a>
### Nested Schema for `vulnerability_found`

Optional:

- `level` (String) The minimum vulnerability severity level that triggers the notification. One of: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Negligible, Unknown. When omitted, the notification fires for any severity. These names match the severity labels shown in the Quay UI.


<a id="nestedatt--webhook"></a>
### Nested Schema for `webhook`

Required:

- `url` (String, Sensitive) The URL to POST the notification payload to. Marked sensitive because webhook URLs frequently embed authentication tokens.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by namespace/repo_name/uuid
# The UUID can be found in the Quay UI under Repository Settings → Notifications
terraform import quay_repository_notification.example my-org/my-app/32bb0ef6-ad69-4ccb-b64e-ddbc8bfd444d
```
